Where it began

Roston Chase was born on 22 March 1992 in Christ Church, Barbados. He first played for Barbados in the 2010-11 four-day competition, at 18, but had to wait two seasons for another game. Once he was back, he stayed.

His first first-class hundred, 120 not out against the Windward Islands, came in the 2014-15 season, when he made 534 runs in eight matches. A season later an unbeaten 136 against the Leeward Islands earned him the match award. The West Indies selectors began to take notice.

The player

He made his Test debut against India in July 2016 and made himself at home at once. In his second Test he took five wickets in an innings and then made a hundred to hold off a strong Indian attack, which is a lot to fit into one match. In 2017 his fellow West Indies players voted him their cricketer of the year, and their Test cricketer of the year as well.

By November 2026 he had played 63 Tests, scoring 2,851 runs with six hundreds and 12 fifties, and taking 102 wickets with his off-spin. His best bowling, 8 for 60, came in the fourth innings against England in Barbados in January 2019, in a Test in which he had also made 54.

What made him special

He was a proper all-rounder, the kind captains love because he gives them two players for the price of one. His batting was built on patience. In June 2026, against Sri Lanka, he made 194 and shared a record sixth-wicket stand with Amir Jangoo, the biggest in Test history. Six runs short of a double hundred, he was bowled, which must have stung for a day or two.

His bowling took its time too. He averaged 48.29 with the ball, so he was more a steady worker than a destroyer, but on his day, as England found out in Barbados, he could run through a side.

Away from the middle

Cricket West Indies made him its regional one-day player of the year in 2018, and played one-day and Twenty20 cricket for the West Indies too. He was picked for the T20 World Cups of 2021 and 2024. In May 2025 he was made West Indies Test captain, and by November 2026 he had led the side in 14 Tests.

And finally

Few batters get to set a world record and then grumble about it. Chase had every reason to do both in the same innings against Sri Lanka: a world-record stand for the sixth wicket, and a score of 194.
